note: Found by the nightly fuzz run on 2026-11-11, on main, at 6000 generated pumping cases. A constant test at 6 m3/h with 21 m of drawdown in the first minute and 11 cm over the hour after it: nearly all offset, such as well loss. The Theis curve can only absorb an offset into its storativity, and here the least squares minimum is at a storativity near 1e-365, which no float holds. Each engine walked down that valley until something gave out, and what gave out differed: Python reached the floor and refused the fit for its storativity, while the browser was still walking at its 20000th evaluation and refused it in scipy's words, 'Optimal parameters not found: Number of calls to function has reached maxfev = 20000', a sentence that says nothing to a field officer. Taking the same steps in both engines (pumping-bootstrap-replicate-at-the-floor.json) does not settle it: over thousands of steps the last bit of the arithmetic still decides which end is reached, and it differs between browser releases. Where the drawdown is nearly all offset the fit is the least squares line through the readings, so its storativity is known in closed form, as a logarithm. Both engines now ask the line first (analysis._line_storativity_log10; the same lines in theisFit) and refuse a minimum it puts under 1e-280 before any search, with the sentence about the offset. On 235 generated fits in the line's regime the line's log10 S and the search's agree to 1e-10.
first_divergence: Optimal parameters not found: Number of calls to function has reached maxfev = 20000.
The Theis fit drives the storativity below 1e-280: the drawdown is nearly all an offset the Theis curve does not model, such as well loss, so T and S cannot be fitted to it
